item.title: Toyama Bay Sushi: Where the Bay's Rich Waters Meet the Sushi Counter — Guide
item.description: Toyama Bay is known among Japanese sushi enthusiasts as a premier source of fresh seafood, fed by nutrient-rich currents and an unusually steep underwater topography that brings deep-water and shallow-water species into close proximity, yielding a wide variety of fish and shellfish landed daily at local ports. Sushi in Toyama ranges from affordable conveyor-belt kaiten-zushi restaurants, several of which are considered among the best of their kind in Japan, to high-end sushi counters showcasing the bay’s specialty catches, including shiro-ebi and hotaru-ika alongside more familiar seasonal fish.
